items: A royalty is a claim on revenue, not on profit — and not equity. The investor pays upfront for a contractual right to a fixed percentage of an asset’s revenue, carved out before any cost line; opex, capex and cost inflation stay with the operator. Exposure is to price and volume only — which is the inflation-hedge mechanism.

A ~USD 2tn market on GP estimates, institutionalizing fast. Established sectors: green metals ~USD 260bn, pharma ~USD 185bn, US natural gas ~USD 140bn, music ~USD 70bn; emerging: brands, carbon offsets, sports. These are sizings of everything royalty-like, not investable float. Fund product has moved from closed-end specialists to evergreen platforms.

Between private credit and private equity — until bankruptcy. Typical gross returns of 10-14% vs 8-12% for private credit and 18-22% for buyouts, cash-yielding from day one. In insolvency, position depends entirely on legal form: a property interest (US fee minerals) survives the operator; a contractual claim (many pharma and media royalties) ranks unsecured.

Self-liquidating cash flows make exit optional — and evergreen natural. Royalties can be underwritten hold-for-life; the four exit routes are upside, not requirement. The same feature supplies the internal liquidity, J-curve-free entry and data-anchored NAVs that semi-liquid structures need.

Risk lives in three places, none of them a payment waterfall: revenue sustainability (volume / price), operator going-concern, and contract legal strength. Two portfolio-level risks sit on top — GP-marked valuation and structure mismatch between book duration and redemption terms.

The investable universe is a 2×2 of sector focus × structure. The four funds on which we hold materials fill three cells; liquidity mechanics — monthly NAV vs a four-yearly run-off option vs GP-led secondary sales — differ more than the headline labels suggest.

How it works: an investor either buys an existing royalty or creates a “synthetic” one by funding an operator for a share of future revenue. Illustration (2% gross revenue royalty): price +20% and costs +33% lift the royalty by exactly 20% while operator profit is flat (38.0 → 37.6).

The cut that matters more than sector is the revenue driver: declining annuity (pharma; fully self-liquidating), perpetual / growing (music, fee minerals; value sits in the terminal and needs a buyer or a structure that can hold) and commodity-linked (gas, green metals; volatile with spot, price leg hedgeable).

items: Music is the most institutionalized market, not the largest; every song carries two copyrights (masters and composition). Strategies run from passive (PG: seasoned catalogs, zero value to unreleased music) to active (Primary Wave: cumulative NPS growth of 92% / 76% / 41% on Fund 1 / 2 / 3 catalogs): streaming beta vs marketing alpha that must be re-proven each fund.

Pharma supply is structural: emerging biopharma originates ~72% of new regulatory filings, and royalties are the only capital channel that is simultaneously non-dilutive, operationally light and product-specific. The inflation hedge is structural, not year-by-year — in 2022 CPI of 8.0% outran branded drug price growth of 4.9%.

Exit routes: hold to run-off (the default; requires no market), secondary sale (mature in pharma and mining, developed in music, thin in niche media and sports), operator buy-back, and portfolio exit via securitization, continuation vehicle or listing.

Why evergreen: redemptions can be met from contractual cash flow — HCRx generated ~USD 228mm of 2025 free cash flow on a USD 2bn+ portfolio (~11%) — with no J-curve or vintage lottery, and NAVs anchored on prescription, streaming and production data. Caveat: a perpetual-family book has a low cash-yield share of value, so a redemption run means selling into whatever secondary depth exists.

items: Instrument mix: names are used loosely; cost exposure and insolvency treatment are not interchangeable. Fee minerals are real property (strongest), an ORRI expires with its lease, an NPI carries costs like equity, and synthetic royalties / RBNs are contractual or credit claims.
Legal-strength mix: share of NAV in property-interest form vs contractual claims against operators, by jurisdiction — the loss-given-stress driver that asset-level marketing skips.
Duration and structure fit: weight the book across the three revenue-driver families, then test cash-yield share of value and internal cash-flow coverage against the vehicle’s redemption terms.

Valuation governance: valuer independence, third-party appraisal coverage, input-data frequency and discount-rate policy. Track records built on hypothetical-liquidation NAVs deserve a different weight from realized DPI.
PG’s net return vs asset-level return as the at-cost 2026 vintage seasons — returns are being shaped by fundraising pace, in both directions.
Price discovery in Primary Wave’s sales to the affiliated Brookfield PCV and the independence of the underlying appraisals.
Music catalog multiples and US statutory streaming rates, a regulatory lever directly on the revenue line.

Sports: no royalty fund has yet reached our materials set; watch the gap between franchise-equity valuations and the ~USD 36bn royalty-addressable figure as collegiate structures move toward synthetic royalties.
